says: One person keeps two sources with one authoring home each: ADR decisions authored as Markdown in the repository's docs/adr directory (a repository-authored memory source whose acceptance authority is the repository, registered after the checkout is bound) and personal working rules in a managed collection (a managed Instructions source accepted by the person). Registering a second, managed home with a derived Markdown view for the ADR source's own id is refused with source_home_conflict, so a mutable managed twin can never edit the decisions the repository document owns. The person commits the rules' first revision and lists it in the personal Instructions position with a second revision only staged as a draft, and lists the ADR source in the repository memory position; each position commits with its own head. Composing a session from the repository and personal scopes (preparation.compose) returns a preparation that names both positions at the heads it read and the rules unit at the committed first revision, never the staged draft; reading the personal position afterwards (collection.read at the head it was committed at) returns the same collection unchanged. The preparation is derived: composing writes no position, creates no second editable original, and a staged object is never counted as committed.
